summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, Marburg, and the Manjushree Centre of Tibetan Culture. She served as Käthe-Leichter-Gastprofessorin at Vienna (~2007–2008) and Privatdozentin at Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Promotion and Habilitation at Hamburg, studying under Ludwig Alsdorf. She held posts at Munich (from 1972) and Münster (professor 1971; Chair of Indology 1988–2000).

Aden Kumler is an art historian and archaeologist educated at Chicago, Toronto, Harvard, and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She was an assistant professor at Chicago (2007–2020) before becoming a professor at the University of Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche.

Adheesh A. Sathaye is an Indology scholar who held positions at UC Berkeley (attested 2004) and Chicago (attested 2005). He has served as Associate Professor of Sanskrit Literature and South Asian Folklore at British Columbia (attested 2006–2025).

Adhémard Leclère was a scholar of religious studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Résident de France at Kratie in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and co-founded and served as vice-president of the Société Ethnologique de Paris.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist who studied at Mumbai and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He taught at Rajaram College (1930–1962), served as Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University (1962–1971), and headed the Jaina Chair at Mysore (1971).
Aditya Behl was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He served as Assistant Professor of Hindi and Urdu at UC Berkeley (~1995–2000) and Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~2001–2009).

Adolf Attenhofer was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Zurich, Geneva, Paris, Berlin, and Munich (under Ernst Kuhn). He taught at Bündner Kantonsschule (~1912–1947) and was the founding director of Bündner Volkshochschule (1924).
Adolf Erhart was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Václav Machek at Masaryk University's Faculty of Arts (~1945–1949). He later served as Professor at Masaryk University from 1988 to 1993.

Adolf Erman was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied under Georg Ebers at Leipzig and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Egyptian Museum of Berlin (~1883–1914) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1923).
Adolf Faust was an Indologist and linguist who received his Ph.D. from the University of Strasbourg in 1877 and worked as a school-teacher (Professor) at Gymnasium Mulhouse.

Adolf Friedrich, an Indologist and historian/archaeologist, earned his Ph.D. at Frankfurt under Leo Frobenius and Hermann Lommel. He held posts at Vienna (PD 1942), Mainz (PD 1946), and Goethe University Frankfurt (~1947–1952).
Adolf Friedrich Hermann Paul Gärtchen was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Breslau (1900–1905), where he studied under Otto Hoffmann and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Berlin (PhD under Bopp), Bonn, and Paris. He served as professor (1833–1847) and Rektor (1862–1863) at the University of Breslau.
Adolf Friedrich von Schack was an Indologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who completed law studies at the universities of Bonn, Heidelberg, and Berlin between 1833 and 1838.

Adolf Holtzmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle, Berlin, Munich, and Paris under scholars including Schleiermacher, Frank, Schmeller, and Burnouf. He taught at Bismarck-Gymnasium Karlsruhe (1837) and was professor at Heidelberg (1852–1870).

Adolf Holtzmann Jr. was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Holtzmann at Heidelberg, Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen, and Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He was a professor of Sanskrit at the University of Freiburg (1885–1914).

Adolf Janáček was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. studies at Charles University (~1920–1925), where he also studied across several faculties and the Examination Board for Teachers at Secondary Schools.

Adolf Kaegi was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich, Leipzig, and Tübingen, learning under Schweizer-Sidler and Roth. He taught at Kantonsschule Rämibühl and was a professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at Zurich (1875–1914).
